candidates.source_attribution: Jubilees 46:1 (Egypt sojourn (46:1)), trans. R.H. Charles, The Book of Jubilees (Oxford: Clarendon, 1902). PD.
candidates.draft_body:
Jubilees (Ethiopian tradition) Book of Jubilees (Mäṣḥafä Kufāle) (c. 150 BC)

'And it came to pass that after Jacob died the children of Israel multiplied in the land of Egypt, and they became a great nation, and they were all of one heart, so that brother loved brother and every man helped his brother, and they increased abundantly and multiplied exceedingly, even for ten weeks of years' — the proto-ecclesial harmony of Israel in early Egypt. Tewahedo ecclesiological theology (the goal of one-heart-and-one-soul, parallel to Acts 4:32) reads this verse as the OT type: harmonious community precedes persecution in the divine pattern, just as church-harmony before persecution.

The pattern (the persecutor of the covenant-people is also a wider regional aggressor) is canonically established. Tewahedo political-theology distinguishes legitimate-defensive-war from imperial-aggressive-war: the pharaoh of the persecution is also the pharaoh of regional-imperial-aggression. The two are not coincidentally co-occurring but causally linked: the covenant-amnesiac is also the regional-imperial-aggressor. The Tewahedo's resistance to Mussolini's 1936 invasion was framed in exactly this canonical category — the imperial-aggressor of 1936 was also the persecutor-of-Tewahedo-Christianity in occupied territory.
